title: 15. System Design Case Studies: Design Zomato
summary: Design Zomato at the scale of ~80 M monthly active users, 200 000+ restaurant partners, and 2 M+ daily delivery orders across ~1 000 Indian cities: restaurant discovery with geospatial search, food ordering & delivery,…
objectives: Step 3: Deep Dive — Data Model (10 min)
Step 4: Deep Dive — Key Algorithms & APIs (10 min)

sections.title: Step 1: Clarify Requirements (5 min)
sections.body:
> **In one line:** Design Zomato at the scale of ~80 M monthly active users, 200 000+ restaurant partners, and 2 M+ daily delivery orders across ~1 000 Indian cities: **restaurant discovery** with **geospatial search**, **food ordering & delivery**, **real-time order tracking**, **ratings & reviews**, **payment** (UPI/cards/wallets), and **dine-out** bookings. Focus on the **geospatial index** for nearby restaurants (S2/geohash), the **order state machine** (placed → accepted → prepared → picked up → delivered), and the **dispatch algorithm** that matches delivery partners to orders. ---

### Functional Requirements
- **Restaurant discovery**: user enters location (or GPS), sees a list of nearby restaurants sorted by relevance (distance, rating, popularity, delivery time). Supports search by cuisine, dish name, restaurant name.
- **Menu browsing**: each restaurant exposes a structured menu (categories, items, price, Veg/Non-veg flag, add-ons, customisations).
- **Cart & order placement**: user adds items, applies coupon, chooses delivery/dine-out, picks payment method, confirms order. Shows ETA + bill breakdown.
- **Order lifecycle**: `placed → restaurant_accepted → preparing → ready_for_pickup → picked_up → en_route → delivered` (plus `cancelled`, `refunded`).
- **Delivery partner dispatch**: system auto-assigns a nearby rider once the restaurant accepts; rider picks up, navigates, delivers.
- **Real-time tracking**: user & restaurant see rider location; rider sees pickup & drop-off locations. Updated every 5–10 s.
- **Ratings & reviews**: post-delivery ratings (1–5 stars) for food, delivery, packaging; text reviews with photos.
- **Payments**: UPI, credit/debit card, NetBanking, wallets (Paytm, PhonePe, Amazon Pay), COD (cash on delivery).
- **Dine-out / Zomato Gold**: table reservation, prepaid dining offers, pay-bill at restaurant.
- **Push notifications**: order status updates, promo alerts, rider arrival.
- **Restaurant partner app**: accept/reject orders, update menu, mark items out-of-stock, view analytics.
- **Rider partner app**: go-online, accept/reject assignments, navigate, mark delivered.

### Non-Functional Requirements
- **Availability** 99.95% (≈ 4.4 h downtime/year) for the order pipeline; discovery & search can be 99.9%.
- **Latency**: discovery API p99 < 300 ms; order placement p99 < 1 s; rider location update p99 < 500 ms.
- **Scale**: 80 M MAU, 200 K restaurants, 2 M orders/day (peak ~5× during dinner 7–9 PM), 1.5 M+ delivery partners.
- **Throughput**: ~10 K orders/min at peak dinner; ~500 K location updates/min from online riders.
- **Storage**: 2 M orders/day × ~20 KB metadata = 40 GB/day metadata; trip GPS tracks ~2 MB each = 4 TB/day. 5-year retention for analytics.
- **Geospatial**: "nearest 50 restaurants within 5 km" in < 100 ms against a 200 K-restaurant index.
- **Consistency**: strong for order state machine (a single order must have one canonical status); eventual for menu/price (a few seconds lag from partner app to user app is fine).
- **Multi-city**: data residency for India (all data stays in Indian AWS/Azure regions); multi-region active-active across Mumbai + Hyderabad DCs.

### Back-of-Envelope Estimation
- **Discovery QPS**: 80 M MAU × 10 sessions/month × 5 discovery calls/session ÷ 30 days È 86 400 s ≈ 1.5 K QPS avg, ~7.5 K QPS at peak.
- **Geospatial index**: 200 K restaurants × 1 row in Redis GEO ≈ 50 MB total (lat, lon, id). `GEORADIUS` lookup of 50 nearest in 5 km ≈ 5 ms.
- **Order creation**: 2 M/day ÷ 86 400 ≈ 23 orders/s avg, ~120 orders/s peak dinner (5×).
- **Location updates**: 1.5 M riders, but only ~500 K online at peak × 1 ping/5 s = 100 K pings/s globally.
- **Trip storage**: 2 M trips/day × 2 MB GPS = 4 TB/day → ~1.5 PB/year. Hot 30 days → SSD; older → S3/Glacier.
- **CDN**: restaurant images, menu thumbnails, review photos — ~50 TB served/day, CloudFront/Akamai.

### Scope
- **In scope**: discovery (geospatial), menu, ordering, dispatch (rider matching), tracking, ratings, payments, scaling, multi-region.
- **Out of scope**: Hyperpure (B2B supply to restaurants), Zomato Landline/Events, marketing campaigns, fraud ML (mention only), full maps/routing (use Mapbox/Google Maps), recommendation ranking model (treat as black box).

sections.title: Step 2: High-Level Architecture (10 min)
sections.body:
### Components 1. **Global DNS + CDN** (Route 53 + CloudFront/Akamai) — routes app to nearest regional API, serves static images and menu thumbnails. 2. **API Gateway** (Kong/Envoy) — TLS, OAuth/JWT, rate limiting, request routing, mobile-vs-web fan-out. 3. **Microservices** (modular monolith split): - **User service**: profile, addresses, preferences, dietary tags. - **Restaurant service**: restaurant catalog, hours, serviceability (does Zomato deliver here?), geo-coding. - **Menu service**: structured menus, items, add-ons, pricing, inventory (out-of-stock). - **Discovery/Search service**: geospatial query + ranking (Elasticsearch or in-house; Redis GEO for "nearby"). - **Order service**: state machine for orders. - **Dispatch service**: matches a rider to an order; the core algorithm. - **Geolocation service**: stores rider live positions in Redis GEO; supports `GEORADIUS`. - **Rider service**: rider profile, vehicle, onboarding, status (online/offline/busy). - **Pricing & coupon service**: bill calculation, taxes (GST 5%), packaging fee, delivery fee, surge delivery fee, discounts. - **ETA service**: predicts food prep time + rider travel time using ML (XGBoost on historical patterns + road graph). - **Payment service**: integrates Razorpay/Juspay/Pine Labs for UPI/cards; COD ledger. - **Rating & review service**: post-delivery ratings, moderation, review aggregation. - **Notification service**: FCM/APNS push, SMS (MSG91), WhatsApp business. 4. **Geospatial index** — Redis GEO (sorted set on geohash) for live riders; Elasticsearch geo_point for restaurant catalog (supports rich filters). 5. **Kafka** — event backbone. Topics: `order-events`, `rider-location`, `restaurant-events`, `payment-events`. Consumers: dispatch, analytics, fraud, surge. 6. **Cassandra** — orders metadata, trip GPS tracks, ratings (high write throughput, multi-region). 7. **MySQL/Aurora** — transactional data (payments, refunds, partner balances, restaurant master). 8. **Redis** — geospatial index, rider status, surge cache, session cart, menu cache. 9. **Elasticsearch** — restaurant search with geo filter, dish search, autocomplete. 10. **ClickHouse** — analytics warehouse (orders, GMV, partner performance, city dashboards). 11. **WebSocket gateway** — streams rider location to user & restaurant apps. 12. **Mapbox/Google Maps** — third-party routing, ETA baseline. ### Mermaid Diagram ```mermaid flowchart LR U([User App]) --> DNS[Route 53 + CDN] RP([Restaurant App]) --> DNS DP([Rider App]) --> DNS DNS --> GW[API Gateway + WS] GW --> USVC[User svc] GW --> RSVC[Restaurant svc] GW --> MSVC[Menu svc] GW --> DISC[Discovery svc] GW --> ORD[Order svc] GW --> WSGW[WebSocket GW] GW --> PAY[Payment svc] WSGW --> U WSGW --> RP WSGW --> DP DP -->|ping every 5s| LOC[Geolocation svc] LOC --> GEO[(Redis GEO
rider index)] DISC --> ES[(Elasticsearch
restaurants geo)] DISC --> MREDIS[(Redis
menu cache)] U -->|place order| ORD ORD --> DISP[Dispatch svc] DISP --> GEO DISP --> ETA[ETA svc] DISP --> RSVC2[Rider svc] RSVC2 -->|offer ride| DP DP -->|accept| RSVC2 RSVC2 --> ORD ORD --> K1[(Kafka: order-events)] LOC --> K2[(Kafka: rider-location)] K1 --> PAY K1 --> NOTIF[Notification svc] K1 --> AN[(ClickHouse analytics)] K2 --> MM[Map matching] K2 --> SURGE[Delivery surge svc] SURGE --> SC[(Redis surge cache)] PAY --> PG[(Razorpay / Juspay)] PAY --> DB[(MySQL payments)] ORD --> CASS[(Cassandra orders + GPS)] ``` ### ASCII Diagram ``` +-------------------+ +-------------------+ +-------------------+ | User App | | Restaurant App | | Rider App | | (browse, order) | | (accept, menu) | | (ping, deliver) | +---+-----------+---+ +---+-----------+---+ +---+-----------+---+ | | | | | | REST | | WS | REST | WS | ping | WS v v v v v v +-----+-----------+----------------+-----------+----------------+-----------+----+ | API Gateway / WebSocket Gateway (per region) | +--+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+----+ | | | | | | | | | | | | v v v v v v v v v v v v +------+--+ ++ +--+---+ ++ +--+---+ ++ +--+--+ ++ +--+--+ ++ +--+--+ ++ +-----+ |User | |Menu| |Rest.| |Disc.| |Order| |Rider| |Pay | |Notif| |svc | |svc | |svc | |svc | |svc | |svc | |svc | |svc | +--------+ +----+ +-----+ +--+--+ +--+--+ +-----+ +----+ +-----+ | | | v v v +---+---+ +--+----+ +-+------+ | Elastic| |Dispatch| |Razorpay| |search | |svc | |gateway | |(geo) | +--+--+--+ +--------+ +--------+ | | ^ | | | +----+ +----+ | v v +---+----+--+ +-----+--------+ |Redis GEO | |Redis GEO | |restaurants| |live riders | +----------+ +-------------+ ^ | (rider pings every 5s) Order state machine: placed -> restaurant_accepted -> preparing -> ready_for_pickup -> picked_up -> en_route -> delivered ``` ### Request Flow Walkthrough 1. **User opens app**: App sends `GET /api/v1/discovery?lat=..&lon=..&q=` → discovery service queries Elasticsearch with a `geo_distance` filter (5 km radius), applies ranking (popularity, rating, ad boosts, time-of-day), returns ~50 restaurants in < 300 ms. Menu thumbnails cached at CDN. 2. **User taps restaurant**: `GET /api/v1/restaurants/{id}/menu` → menu service returns structured menu from Redis cache (TTL 60 s). If a partner just updated stock, cache invalidation via Kafka `restaurant-events` topic. 3. **User places order**: `POST /api/v1/orders` → order service validates cart against menu/stock, calculates bill (pricing service), reserves payment (Razorpay order ID), persists order in Cassandra in `placed` state, publishes `order-placed` event to Kafka. 4. **Restaurant accepts**: Restaurant partner app receives push (FCM). On accept, `order-accepted` event → order state `restaurant_accepted` → `preparing`. ETA service recomputes delivery ETA. 5. **Dispatch**: When order is `preparing`, dispatch service is invoked. It computes pickup ETA, queries Redis GEO for nearest online riders within ~2 km, filters by vehicle type & on-time score, picks top 3 candidates. Sends an assignment offer via WebSocket to the highest-ranked rider; rider has 10 s to accept. If declined, next candidate. 6. **Rider picks up**: Rider navigates to restaurant (Mapbox routing), marks `picked_up`. State → `picked_up` → `en_route`. WebSocket streams rider location to user & restaurant every 5 s. 7. **Delivery**: Rider navigates to drop-off, marks `delivered`. State → `delivered`. Payment captured. Rating prompt shown. 8. **Surge**: Delivery surge service consumes `order-placed` & `rider-online` events, computes supply/demand per hexagon (H3 level 8), updates `surge_multiplier` in Redis. Pricing service uses it for delivery fee.

sections.title: Step 3: Deep Dive — Data Model (10 min)
sections.body:
### Tables / Schema

**MySQL — `restaurants`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE restaurants (
    restaurant_id      BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    name               VARCHAR(200),
    chain_id           BIGINT,
    cuisine_tags       JSON,             -- ["North Indian","Chinese"]
    lat                DECIMAL(10,7),
    lon                DECIMAL(10,7),
    city_id            INT,
    locality           VARCHAR(100),
    avg_rating         DECIMAL(3,2),
    rating_count       INT,
    is_veg_only        BOOLEAN,
    cost_for_two       INT,
    is_active          BOOLEAN,
    delivery_enabled   BOOLEAN,
    created_at         TIMESTAMP
);
```

**MySQL — `menu_items`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE menu_items (
    item_id            BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    restaurant_id      BIGINT,
    category           VARCHAR(50),       -- Starters, Mains, Desserts
    name               VARCHAR(200),
    description        TEXT,
    price              DECIMAL(8,2),
    is_veg             BOOLEAN,
    in_stock           BOOLEAN,
    display_order      INT,
    add_ons            JSON,
    INDEX idx_restaurant (restaurant_id, display_order)
);
```

**Cassandra — `orders`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE orders (
    order_id           UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id            UUID,
    restaurant_id      UUID,
    rider_id           UUID,
    pickup_lat         DOUBLE,
    pickup_lon         DOUBLE,
    drop_lat           DOUBLE,
    drop_lon           DOUBLE,
    status             TEXT,             -- placed|accepted|preparing|ready|picked_up|en_route|delivered|cancelled
    items              TEXT,             -- JSON snapshot
    subtotal           DECIMAL,
    delivery_fee       DECIMAL,
    taxes              DECIMAL,
    discount           DECIMAL,
    total              DECIMAL,
    payment_method     TEXT,             -- upi|card|wallet|cod
    surge_mult         DOUBLE,
    placed_at          TIMESTAMP,
    delivered_at       TIMESTAMP
);
```

**Cassandra — `order_tracking` (GPS trace)**
```sql
CREATE TABLE order_tracking (
    order_id    UUID,
    ts          TIMESTAMP,
    lat         DOUBLE,
    lon         DOUBLE,
    heading     DOUBLE,
    speed       DOUBLE,
    rider_id    UUID,
    PRIMARY KEY (order_id, ts)
) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY (ts ASC);
```

**Cassandra — `reviews`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE reviews (
    review_id          UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    order_id           UUID,
    user_id            UUID,
    restaurant_id      UUID,
    rider_id           UUID,
    food_rating        TINYINT,          -- 1..5
    delivery_rating    TINYINT,
    packaging_rating   TINYINT,
    text_review        TEXT,
    photo_urls         SET<TEXT>,
    created_at         TIMESTAMP,
    is_flagged         BOOLEAN
);
```

**Redis GEO key — `riders:online:{city}`**
```
GEOADD riders:online:mumbai 72.8777 19.0760 "rider_1234"
GEORADIUS riders:online:mumbai 72.8777 19.0760 2 km COUNT 10 ASC
```

### Indexes
- MySQL `restaurants`: composite (city_id, is_active), full-text on name for admin search, spatial covered by Elasticsearch.
- Elasticsearch `restaurants`: `geo_point` field for `lat,lon`; `bool` filter for veg/cuisine; `function_score` for popularity/rating.
- Cassandra: queries are by `order_id` (PK) and by `user_id` → denormalised `orders_by_user` table with `(user_id, placed_at)` partition.
- Redis GEO: O(log N) radius scan; the index is naturally sorted by geohash.

### Storage Choice
- **Cassandra** for orders/tracking: high write throughput (100 K pings/s), multi-region replication, time-series access pattern.
- **MySQL** for restaurants/menu/users: ACID for catalog edits; reads fan out via Elasticsearch & Redis caches.
- **Elasticsearch** for discovery: combines geo filter + ranking + full-text. Heavier than pure Redis GEO but enables complex queries.
- **Redis** for live rider positions, surge cache, menu cache (read-heavy, TTL-based).
- **S3 + CloudFront** for restaurant images, menu thumbnails, review photos.

sections.title: Step 4: Deep Dive — Key Algorithms & APIs (10 min)
sections.body:
### API Design
```
GET  /api/v1/discovery?lat&lon&q&cuisine&veg&sort&page
GET  /api/v1/restaurants/{id}
GET  /api/v1/restaurants/{id}/menu
POST /api/v1/cart/items                  {item_id, qty, add_ons}
POST /api/v1/orders                      {cart, address_id, payment_method, coupon}
GET  /api/v1/orders/{id}
POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel
POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/rate            {food, delivery, packaging, text}
GET  /api/v1/orders/{id}/track           (or via WebSocket)
WS   /ws/v1/track/{order_id}             rider location stream
POST /api/v1/rider/online
POST /api/v1/rider/location              {lat, lon, heading}
POST /api/v1/rider/assignment/{id}/accept
POST /api/v1/rider/assignment/{id}/reject
POST /api/v1/restaurants/{id}/orders/{order_id}/accept
POST /api/v1/restaurants/{id}/orders/{order_id}/ready
```

### Key Algorithms

**Dispatch — nearest rider matching with ETA weighting**
```python
import heapq, math

def haversine_km(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):
    R = 6371.0
    p1, p2 = math.radians(lat1), math.radians(lat2)
    dphi = math.radians(lat2 - lat1)
    dlmb = math.radians(lon2 - lon1)
    a = math.sin(dphi/2)**2 + math.cos(p1)*math.cos(p2)*math.sin(dlmb/2)**2
    return 2 * R * math.asin(math.sqrt(a))

def find_candidate_riders(redis_geo, pickup_lat, pickup_lon, radius_km=2.0, limit=20):
    """Query Redis GEO for online riders near pickup."""
    raw = redis_geo.georadius(
        "riders:online", pickup_lon, pickup_lat, radius_km,
        unit="km", withcoord=True, withdist=True, count=limit, sort="ASC")
    return [{
        "rider_id": r[0].decode(),
        "dist_km":  r[1],
        "lat":      r[2][1],
        "lon":      r[2][0],
    } for r in raw]

def score_rider(rider, pickup_lat, pickup_lon, eta_lookup, rider_stats):
    """Lower score = better candidate. Blends ETA, on-time %, idle time."""
    eta_min = eta_lookup(rider["rider_id"], rider["lat"], rider["lon"],
                         pickup_lat, pickup_lon)        # via mapbox / ETA svc
    on_time = rider_stats.get(rider["rider_id"], {}).get("on_time_pct", 0.9)
    idle_min = rider_stats.get(rider["rider_id"], {}).get("idle_min", 5)
    # weighted: emphasise ETA, penalise low on-time, gently reward longer idle
    return (eta_min * 0.7
            + (1 - on_time) * 20.0
            + max(0, 10 - idle_min) * 0.1)

def dispatch(redis_geo, pickup_lat, pickup_lon, eta_lookup, rider_stats,
             assigner, max_attempts=3):
    """Core dispatch: pick best rider, offer; on reject/timeout, try next."""
    candidates = find_candidate_riders(redis_geo, pickup_lat, pickup_lon)
    if not candidates:
        return None
    # rank by composite score
    scored = [(score_rider(c, pickup_lat, pickup_lon, eta_lookup, rider_stats),
               c) for c in candidates]
    heapq.heapify(scored)
    for _ in range(max_attempts):
        if not scored:
            return None
        _, rider = heapq.heappop(scored)
        ok = assigner.offer(rider["rider_id"], timeout_s=10)   # WS push
        if ok:
            return rider
    return None   # escalate: increase radius, broadcast to fleet
```

**Order state machine (guard transitions)**
```python
VALID_TRANSITIONS = {
    "placed":             {"accepted", "cancelled"},
    "accepted":           {"preparing", "cancelled"},
    "preparing":          {"ready_for_pickup", "cancelled"},
    "ready_for_pickup":   {"picked_up"},
    "picked_up":          {"en_route"},
    "en_route":           {"delivered"},
    "delivered":          {},
    "cancelled":          {},
}

def transition(current, next_state):
    if next_state not in VALID_TRANSITIONS.get(current, set()):
        raise InvalidTransition(f"{current} -> {next_state}")
    return next_state
```

sections.title: Step 5: Scalability & Reliability (5 min)
sections.body:
### Scaling Challenges
- **Dinner peak (7–9 PM)**: 5× normal QPS. Auto-scale stateless services on Kubernetes (HPA on CPU + custom QPS metric). Pre-warm cache (popular restaurants, menus) at 6 PM. Over-provision dispatch workers.
- **Geospatial index hot spots**: a single Redis GEO key for all of Mumbai gets hammered. Shard by H3 hexagon level 8 — one key per cell (~1 km²). Riders belong to one cell at a time; cross-cell dispatch falls back to scanning neighbours.
- **Rider location write fan-in**: 100 K pings/s → single Redis is borderline. Use Redis Cluster (16 shards), pipelined writes, and a Kafka spout so the ingestion path is durable.
- **Multi-region active-active**: orders placed in Mumbai DC stay in Mumbai; Hyderabad DC serves southern cities. Cassandra `NetworkTopologyStrategy` with RF=3 per DC. Cross-region traffic only for partner master data (restaurants, menus) — replicated via Kafka MirrorMaker2.
- **Order state machine integrity**: one canonical owner — order service, persisted in Cassandra with LWT (lightweight transaction) for transition. Redis cache holds the latest state for fast reads.

### Caching Strategy
- **Restaurant list by geo cell**: Redis cache keyed `cell:{h3_id}:restaurants` TTL 5 min. Cache-aside.
- **Menu**: Redis `menu:{restaurant_id}` TTL 60 s. Invalidated on partner menu update via Kafka event.
- **Discovery results**: CDN edge cache for popular searches (e.g. "biryani near Koramangala") for 30 s.
- **Rider live position**: Redis GEO (in-memory, hot).
- **Surge**: Redis `surge:{h3_id}` TTL 5 min, refreshed by surge consumer.

### Failure Modes
- **Restaurant partner app offline during dinner**: order auto-accept fallback (if restaurant opted in). Else order cancelled within 90 s + user refunded.
- **Rider rejects / no rider available**: dispatch widens radius (2 km → 4 km → 6 km), then broadcasts to fleet (push "earn ₹X bonus"). If still no rider in 8 min, mark `unassignable` and refund.
- **Redis GEO down**: fallback to Elasticsearch `geo_distance` query (slower but durable) or to a precomputed rider bucket in Cassandra.
- **Cassandra quorum failure**: order writes block — circuit breaker returns `503` to user app, which retries with exponential backoff. Active-active failover to other DC.
- **Payment gateway timeout**: idempotency key prevents double-charge; reconcile via webhook from Razorpay + nightly batch.
- **Kafka broker loss**: replicas cover (RF=3); producers get `LEADER_NOT_AVAILABLE` for ~1 s, retried transparently.
- **Map service outage**: ETA service falls back to haversine distance ÷ avg city speed; routing returns polyline from cached historical route.

quiz.question: How does Zomato find "nearby restaurants" fast at scale?
options: The order is in placed state with payment captured. Safeguards: (1) Accept SLA: order service has a 90-second timer from placed.
The order placement API requires an idempotency key (Idempotency-Key header, UUID generated by the client).
Three layers of impact. (1) Dispatch degradation: the Redis GEO index has stale positions; GEORADIUS returns riders whose real position is unknown.
Zomato uses a geospatial index — Redis GEO for live rider positions and Elasticsearch with a geo_point field for the restaurant catalog.

Redis GEO is internally a sorted set keyed on geohash, so a GEORADIUS query is O(log N + M) where M is the result size. For discovery, the request includes the user's lat/lon; Elasticsearch applies a geo_distance filter (e.g.

quiz.question: How does the dispatch algorithm avoid assigning the same rider to two orders?
options: Two problems: cache invalidation storm and write contention on MySQL.

For each H3 hexagon (level 8, ~0.7 km²), it computes demand = orders_in_window and supply = avg_online_riders. The multiplier M = clamp(1.0 + 0.5 * log2(demand / supply), 1.0, 2.5) if demand > supply, else 1.0.

Two problems: cache invalidation storm and write contention on MySQL.

The two workloads are fundamentally different.
quiz.explanation: The two workloads are fundamentally different. Orders have a high write rate (~120/s peak), time-series access (most reads are recent orders by user_id), grow unboundedly (~30 M orders/year per region), and tolerate eventual consistency across regions. Cassandra's append-only LSM-tree storage, partition-key access pattern, and tunable consistency fit perfectly.
